resumeByTaskKey: Same taskKey, closed episode still in state: startEpisode (external-controller.ts:704) finds it with no closedAt check, sets sessionHeads[session] to it and returns it with closedAt set. No new episode, no reopen, no successor, no event. workflowNext on the start result is hard-coded status 'active' (controller-learning-tools.ts:150-158). Afterwards every task-bound write is refused or dropped: learning checkpoint/review/receipt throw LEARNING_EXTERNAL_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE (invocationTaskCurrent false), memory_v2 admission throws MEMORY_CONTROLLER_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE, planned context returns scope-unavailable, tool events become late-closed, and episode verify silently returns without recording anything. Same taskKey, archived episode: recentEpisodes supplies it as 'prior' (line 700), it is pushed back into state (705), the head is set (706) and the closed body is returned; the same mutate's save() re-archives it (closed, !pending, length>128), so the head dangles and linkMemoryTask reports EXTERNAL_CONTINUITY_STALE_TASK. Later calls are unbound ('no-task'), and the reconnect path is blocked because the head exists. Repeating start with the same taskKey loops; only a new taskKey creates a working episode, and the old one becomes its predecessor. This is already how legitimately closed (terminalOutcome) episodes behave today (99 of 100 current archive files have terminalOutcome); live state shows 29 of 191 sessionHeads already pointing at archive-only episodes. Tests cover archive reconnect only for NON-closed episodes with fewer than 128 episodes (tests/memory/memory-task-binding.test.ts:86,105).
evaluatorInputs: evaluateExternalComparison, projectExternalFeatureOutcomes and externalFeatureOutcomeProposals (src/learning/external-evaluation.ts) are pure functions of the arrays their caller passes; they never touch disk and never read closedAt. They use only id, startedAt, terminalOutcome and verificationStatus, so rules A/B (terminalOutcome unset, verificationStatus 'unavailable') do not change their outcome classification. The callers differ. evaluate() (external-controller.ts:1935) uses recentEpisodes, which unions state.episodes with every episodes-archive/*.json, so it loses nothing; only the limit cap (4-100, default 40) applies. status().featureOutcomeEvidence (2030-2031) and curate() (1994-1998) use state.episodes only and also filter tracker events to tasks present in state, so archived episodes and their feature-outcome events vanish: groups shrink and curator proposals (need total>=2 and |score|>=0.25) can disappear. Also lost on archive: the health/status episodeCount (display only), and any state-only scan (releaseClosedCheckpoints, recordLearningReview, procedure migration workspace derivation). Procedure support/failure episode ids live in LearningService as plain strings with no lookup into the external state (procedureBoundEvidence is receipt-based), so they are unaffected; live state.procedures is empty.
verdict: Yes: rules A/B change externally observable behavior well beyond file size, mainly rule A. Closure has no reopen path, and MEMORY_EPISODES=128 never binds for closed episodes here (603 episodes, 204 pending), so every closed non-pending episode is archived at the same save; 'closed in state' is transient. Live counts (inference, using updatedAt as the activity proxy): about 152 episodes with learningDecision and no terminalOutcome would close, of which 85 explicit ones were updated within 7 days and 134 are explicit taskKey-bound; rule B adds 107 inferred episodes at 7 days idle (12 at 14, 0 at 30), which no bound consumer uses. Today reviewed-but-unverified episodes stay open and resumable. After the rule, an old taskKey cannot be resumed (start re-adopts the closed episode and then re-archives it, leaving a dangling head), episode verify after review silently no-ops, a second checkpoint/review cycle is refused, improvement register/feedback/progress follow-ups, procedure list/inspect, Memory v2 read/write admission, planned context, reconstruction_harness and artifact_inspect are refused, and skill-proposal reminders and capability notices are suppressed. skill-proposal-actions also falls back to workspace 'agent-core' for a dangling head, and an orphan Learning checkpoint of an archived task becomes unreleasable. Archive also drops episodes from status().featureOutcomeEvidence, curate() and health episodeCount, while evaluate() and resolveMemoryTask() still see them via the archive. Callers at risk: controllers that reuse a taskKey across chats or days, long-lived mcp-session-id sessions idle over 24h, and any user-decision follow-up on an improvement or proposal. Low risk: rule B alone and display-only consumers. An unwanted-exposure fix would be to make startEpisode treat a closed match as a predecessor of a fresh episode (or reopen it) and to skip session heads when archiving; this is a suggestion, not verified.
openQuestions: Where would the rule run (every save() or a separate sweep) and how is 'session active within 24h' measured? sessionHeads has no timestamps; updatedAt of the head episode is the only available proxy. Live: 191 heads (164 distinct), 15 point to episodes updated within 24h, 29 already dangle to archive-only episodes.

Do real clients reuse one mcp-session-id for more than 24h? Header present gives a stable session id (mcp/handler.ts:67-79); header-less clients rotate hourly. This decides how often an idle-then-resumed session hits the dangling-head path.

One current open episode (id starting ext-031299db, explicit, taskKey set, a session head) also has an archive file without closedAt; it is unknown which build wrote that file. It is consistent with startEpisode rehydration but not proven.

A rehydrated episode leaves its archive file in place and re-archive overwrites it (with .last-good), so the archive can hold stale duplicates. recentEpisodes resolves duplicates by letting state win.

Existing tests encode only terminalOutcome-based closure (tests/cumulative-workflow.test.ts:118, tests/memory/memory-task-reconnect.test.ts:411, tests/batch16-exact-task-verification.test.ts:79, tests/learning-external-scope.test.ts:89, tests/external-reconstruction-harness.test.ts:244,272). None covers startEpisode on a closed or archived taskKey with more than 128 episodes, nor rule A/B closure.

recentEpisodes scans the whole archive directory per call and fails entirely on one unreadable file (line 1224); archive count would go from 100 to roughly 350 on the live data. Not measured; cost estimate is 10 KB average per episode (measured on state: about 10,108 bytes).
